picks.editorial_note: A combined $1.1B+ commitment from Georgia Tech and Emory is one of the largest university AI investments of the year, positioning the state as a national AI hub and signaling how seriously research universities are betting on AI infrastructure.
picks.title: Georgia Tech and Emory Invest More Than $1B in AI to Drive State’s Jobs, Economic Growth

picks.editorial_note: A White House-backed consortium uniting 15 universities across 10 states to share supercomputing resources marks a significant federal push to regionalize AI research infrastructure, with ripple effects for every participating institution.
picks.title: UK partners with regional universities in super intelligence computing consortium

picks.editorial_note: SLAC's leadership of a DOE Genesis Mission project applying AI-driven autonomous discovery to catalysis could accelerate breakthroughs in energy chemistry, exemplifying the government's growing bet on 'self-driving science.'
picks.title: SLAC to lead a Department of Energy Genesis Mission project for Super Intelligence (SI)-driven autonomous discovery in catalysis

picks.editorial_note: Fermilab's two new Genesis Mission awards apply AI to microelectronics design and quantum information science, two fields central to next-generation computing and national competitiveness.
picks.title: Fermilab to lead two new Genesis Mission awards to accelerate development of microelectronics and quantum

picks.editorial_note: Phase II DOE funding for Berkeley Lab's AI-driven particle accelerator design project shows sustained federal investment in using AI to push the frontiers of physics instrumentation.
picks.title: Super Intelligence for Particle Accelerators Gets Another Boost

picks.editorial_note: SLAC's SPIRE project aims to build fully autonomous 'self-driving laboratories' where AI agents and robots run experiments independently, a significant step toward automating the scientific method itself.
picks.title: SLAC leads new project to build the self-driving laboratory of the future

picks.editorial_note: Georgia Tech's $20M NSF-funded Nexus supercomputer, built in partnership with UIUC and opened to researchers nationwide, expands the national AI compute infrastructure available to the broader research community.
picks.title: Georgia Tech Opens Supercomputer to Researchers Nationwide

picks.editorial_note: A $30M NSF center spanning Indiana, UT Austin, MIT, Tufts, Utah, and Yale to study human-robot co-adaptation represents a substantial, multi-institution bet on safer and more effective human-AI collaboration.
picks.title: Luddy researchers join new $30 million NSF Center to shape the future of human-robot co-adaptation

picks.editorial_note: A $6M NIH Director's Pioneer Award to build an AI-human discovery engine for cancer research highlights growing federal confidence in LLM-agent-driven biomedical discovery.
picks.title: Dr. Olivier Elemento Wins NIH Director’s Pioneer Award
picks.university: Weill Medical College of Cornell University

picks.editorial_note: A Case Western alumnus's optical computing startup, using light instead of electronic circuits, tackles one of AI's most pressing real-world constraints: the soaring energy cost of running large models.
picks.title: A CWRU entrepreneur studied invisibility cloaks. Now he’s working to cut AI’s energy use | CWRU Newsroom | Case Western Reserve University
